messages:
incident-bot: ⚠️ Alert: p95 latency spike detected for /v1/generate on pool-dedicated-us-east-2 — p95=680ms (baseline 160ms), error-rate +1.2%

maya: seeing the same in dashboards :eyes:

liam: any recent deploys to that pool? tl;dr: no deploys in last 6h

tony: perf deck shows throughput drop too. looks like queueing in runtime

anika: initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor (large batch job) or kernel selection fallback misroute

maya: ran a quick profile on an affected node, pasted top lines:
```
RUNTIME_PROF: kernel_pick: model=redwood-1-small seq=2048 -> selected=matmul_fast (expected=attention_fused)
RUNTIME_PROF: batching_window=100ms -> microbatches=48 -> queue_latency=120ms
KV_CACHE: miss_rate=0.87, evict_rate=12/s, cache_hit=0.13
```

liam: whoa seqlen heuristic picked the wrong kernel for long sequences — matmul_fast is super slow for >1024

sre-oncall: tracing is thin for this route — only 0.1% trace sampling configured, we have ~30k requests/min so most traces dropped :grimacing:

anika: also observability-bot shows the trace-aggregator restarted 4m ago on that cluster (might explain missing spans)

observability-bot: FYI: trace-aggregator (v2.3.1) crashed at 1813456798, restarted by deploy-bot at 1813456812

maya: quick mitigations: 1) pin kernel selection for redwood-1-small to attention_fused for pool-dedicated-us-east-2 2) reduce batching_window to 30ms 3) increase KV cache max-entries on the pool 4) temporarily bump trace sampling for /v1/generate to 1%

deploy-bot: Applying kernel pin (canary) to 2 nodes now. rolling update started.

liam: deployed batching window change to all runtime schedulers for that pool.

tony: cache resize done on three nodes; monitoring hit-rate.

sre-oncall: increased route trace sampling to 1% and bumped trace-aggregator restart handling.

maya: after canary pin and batch change p95 dropped from 680ms -> 210ms on canary nodes, overall pool p95 trending down

anika: root cause notes: seq-length heuristic threshold drifted after a recent metric change (we were using token_count metric from tokenizer v2) causing kernel mis-selection for long inputs -> larger microbatches and KV churn -> tail latency spike. compounding factor: trace sampling too low + aggregator restart = observability gap during peak

maya: follow-ups: (1) add regression test for seqlen->kernel mapping (2) adjust tokenizer metric to be canonical source (3) improve trace-aggregator health checks and fallback buffering (4) re-evaluate default batching_window for long-seq workloads

liam: assigning follow-ups: maya#1, anika#2, sre-oncall#3, tony#4

maya: good to close incident after 2h of stable p95 <250ms. logging postmortem

observability-bot: Incident auto-closed after 2h stable. link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1813456789
